To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a series of novel furo‐[2.3‐b] quinolines with different substituents at C‐6 position were designed and synthesized and their cytotoxicities were evaluated.
the novel furo[3,2‐b]quinolines 7, 8a, and 10a‐10e were synthesized, and their structures were confirmed.

the introduction of benzyl ether and benzene sulfonate to 2‐chloro‐6‐hydroxyl‐furo[2, 3‐b]quionline (2) can significantly improve the cytotoxicity of 2, while the benzenesulfonic ester failed to enhance potency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel furoquinolines as anticancer agents and may serve as the basis for further structure–activity relationship (SAR) studies.
the discovery of novel furo‐[2‐, 3‐]quinoline‐6‐carboxylic acids derivatives as potential cytotoxic agents.
the development of new anticancer agents with furo[2‐3‐b] quinoline as the core structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytotoxicity of these compounds is closely related to the introduction of different groups at 6‐position, the length of alkyl chains, and the substitution position of the benzene rings.
the cytotoxicity of furo[3,2‐b]quinolines is closely related to the substituent at 6‐position.
the cytotoxicity is highly dependent on the structure of the substituents at the C6‐position.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of a benzyl ether or benzenesulfate at 6‐position would be a good strategy to enhance cytotoxicity of furo[3,4‐b]quinolines.

the introduction of benzyl ether and benzene sulfonate to furo[2‐b]quinolines could improve the cytotoxicities, and compound 10c exhibited potent antiproliferation activity and good selectivity, which might be an ideal candidate for further study.
2‐bromo‐6‐hydroxyl‐furo[2, 3‐b]quinaldine derivatives were promising candidates for further study and 10c might have potential as a novel antitumor agent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the introduction of benzyl ether or benzenesulfonic acid could significantly improve the cytotoxicity of the furo[2.3‐b] quinoline skeleton, which provides a reference for the design of novel anticancer drugs.
the introduction of benzyl ether and benzene sulfonate to 7 could enhance its anticancer potency and the selectivity to MCF‐77 and HCT‐16.
the introduction of a benzyl ether or benzenesulfone group at 6‐position could enhance cytotoxicities, which may be used as an important lead structure for the design of novel anticancer drugs.
